title: Long-term ECG monitor (7 to 14 day patch)
what: A small monitor shaped like a sticky patch is placed on your chest. It records your ECG nonstop for 1 to 2 weeks while you live your normal life.
why: When skipped beats, a racing heart, or fainting happen rarely and a 24-hour Holter monitor does not catch them.
duration: it is usually worn for 7 to 14 days; results come a few days after it is removed
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to bandages or adhesive

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day it is put on, do not use cream on your chest. For men, the spot is sometimes shaved.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down the time and what you felt. The patch often has a button. Press it when you have symptoms.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Many patches allow showers, but not baths or swimming. Check for your device.

bring: A notebook or phone for your diary
steps: The nurse cleans the skin on your chest
The patch is stuck on the left side of your chest
The nurse checks that it is recording
You are shown how to press the button and keep a diary
You go home and live as usual
After 7 to 14 days, you remove the patch yourself or at the clinic, as instructed
feel: The skin under the patch may itch
For the first few days you notice it, then you get used to it
after: Return the patch to the clinic or mail it, as instructed
Reading the recording usually takes a few days
Slight redness after removal goes away on its own
red_flags: Severe chest pain, fainting, or trouble breathing: call emergency services. The patch does not get in the way
Severe itching or blisters under the patch: contact the clinic

faq.q: Can I shower with the patch?
faq.a: Many patches can handle it, but baths and pools are usually not allowed. Check for your device.

faq.q: What if the patch comes off?
faq.a: Call the clinic. Do not tape it back on without advice.

reminders.text: Your ECG patch goes on tomorrow. Do not put cream on your chest in the morning. Decide where you will keep your diary.
